## 1. Motor line current

Assumptions:

- The stated 15 kW is the motor’s mechanical output power.
- The 400 V line-to-line value is RMS, as is standard for AC supply ratings.
- The motor operates under balanced three-phase sinusoidal conditions.
- Because the catalogue defines \(I_n\) as the **amplitude** of a sinusoidal current, it is treated as a peak value.

The motor input power is

\[
P_{\text{in}}=\frac{P_{\text{out}}}{\eta}
=\frac{15}{0.90}
=16.6667\ \text{kW}.
\]

For a balanced three-phase motor,

\[
P_{\text{in}}=\sqrt{3}\,U_{LL}\,I_{\text{motor,RMS}}\cos\varphi .
\]

Therefore,

\[
I_{\text{motor,RMS}}
=
\frac{16\,666.7}
{\sqrt{3}(400)(0.84)}
=
28.6384\ \text{A}.
\]

Equivalently,

\[
I_{\text{motor,RMS}}
=
\frac{15\,000}
{\sqrt{3}(400)(0.84)(0.90)}
=
28.6384\ \text{A}.
\]

Convert this RMS current to sinusoidal amplitude:

\[
I_{\text{motor,peak}}
=
\sqrt{2}\,I_{\text{motor,RMS}}
=
\sqrt{2}(28.6384)
=
40.5008\ \text{A}.
\]

## 2. Catalogue selection

For the VL-42:

- Supply window:

\[
380 \le 400 \le 480\ \text{V}
\]

- Output-frequency window:

\[
0 \le 50 \le 60\ \text{Hz}
\]

- Rated power:

\[
22 \ge 15\ \text{kW}
\]

- Output-current amplitude:

\[
46 \ge 40.5008\ \text{A}
\]

The cheaper VL-25 and VL-36 do not satisfy the current requirement because their \(I_n\) values are 33 A and 38 A, respectively, both below 40.5008 A. The VL-60 also qualifies but costs 890 EUR, so the lowest-price qualifying unit is the VL-42 at 640 EUR.

Current relative to the VL-42 rating:

\[
I_{\text{motor,peak}}-I_n
=
40.5008-46
=
-5.4992\ \text{A}.
\]

Thus, the motor-current amplitude is approximately 5.50 A below the inverter rating.

## Results

| Item | Result |
|---|---:|
| selected model | **VL-42** |
| price (EUR) | **640** |
| motor line current (A) | **28.64 A RMS** (**40.50 A peak**) |
| current compared with \(I_n\) (A) | **\(-5.50\) A**, i.e. 5.50 A below \(I_n\) |
| \(I_n\) (A) | **46** |

Assumptions used:
- The motor’s 15 kW is shaft/output power, so the inverter must supply the motor input power \(P_{\text{in}}=P_{\text{out}}/\eta\).
- The 400 V supply and motor voltage are line-to-line RMS values; the current from the three-phase power equation is therefore RMS line current.
- The catalogue defines \(I_n\) as the **amplitude** of permissible sinusoidal output current, so the RMS motor current is converted to peak amplitude using \(I_{\text{pk}}=\sqrt{2}\,I_{\text{rms}}\).
- “Covers” is treated as inclusive.

Calculation:
\[
P_{\text{in}}=\frac{15\text{ kW}}{0.90}=16.6667\text{ kW}=16666.6667\text{ W}
\]

\[
I_{\text{line,rms}}=\frac{P_{\text{in}}}{\sqrt{3}\,U_{LL}\,\cos\varphi}
=\frac{16666.6667}{\sqrt{3}\cdot400\cdot0.84}
\]

\[
\sqrt{3}\cdot400\cdot0.84=581.9690713
\]

\[
I_{\text{line,rms}}=\frac{16666.6667}{581.9690713}=28.6384\text{ A}
\]

Convert to catalogue comparison basis:
\[
I_{\text{compared}}=\sqrt{2}\cdot28.6384=40.5008\text{ A amplitude}
\]

Catalogue screening:
- Supply window: all VL models cover 400 V because \(380\le400\le480\).
- Output frequency: all cover 50 Hz because \(0\le50\le60\).
- Rated power: all cover 15 kW because the smallest \(P_n\) is 18 kW.
- Current: VL-25 has \(I_n=33<40.5008\), fail; VL-36 has \(I_n=38<40.5008\), fail; VL-42 has \(I_n=46\ge40.5008\), pass; VL-60 also passes but costs more.

Final conclusion: the lowest-price VL unit satisfying all conditions is **VL-42** at **EUR 640**, with current margin \(46-40.5008=5.4992\) A.

### Calculation

Assumptions:

- The stated 15 kW is the motor’s mechanical output power.
- Power factor and efficiency apply at the stated operating point.
- The catalogue current \(I_n\) is directly comparable with the calculated motor line current, with no additional derating.
- Voltage and frequency limits are inclusive.

Motor electrical input power:

\[
P_{\text{in}}=\frac{P_{\text{out}}}{\eta}
=\frac{15}{0.90}
=16.6667\ \text{kW}
\]

Motor line current:

\[
I_{\text{motor}}
=\frac{P_{\text{in}}}{\sqrt{3}\,U_{LL}\,\cos\varphi}
=\frac{16\,666.7}{\sqrt{3}(400)(0.84)}
\]

\[
I_{\text{motor}}
=\frac{16\,666.7}{581.969}
=28.64\ \text{A}
\]

For the VL-25:

- Supply window: \(380 \le 400 \le 480\ \text{V}\)
- Frequency window: \(0 \le 50 \le 60\ \text{Hz}\)
- Rated power: \(18 \ge 15\ \text{kW}\)
- Rated current: \(33 \ge 28.64\ \text{A}\)

Current margin:

\[
I_n-I_{\text{motor}}=33-28.64=4.36\ \text{A}
\]

The VL-25 satisfies all requirements and, at EUR 410, is the lowest-priced model in the catalogue.
